To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel method for the odometry estimation from 3D point clouds using convolutional neural nets.

we have proposed a method for odometry and LiDAR registration estimation using 3D LiDar data and CNNs, and that the proposed method achieves significantly better precision in odometry estimation comparing with state of art method LOAM while achieving real-time performances.
* CNN for IMU assisted velodyne LiDar odometry estimation * Real time odometry estimation with high precision
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects:
CNN based odometry estimation using 3D LiDar scans
the improvement of odometry estimation using LiDAR scans, which is one of the key components of the mapping process and the autonomous driving.
the development of CNN-based odometry estimation from sparse 3D Li-DAR point clouds, which is a challenging task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a new method which can replace wheel encoder and GNSS sensor in odometry estimation.
the CNN based method outperforms the state of the art in odometry estimation, while achieving real time performance and high precision.
the proposed method is able to provide high quality odometry data, which are essential to the mapping process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel CNN based method for odometry prediction from 3D point clouds.
we present an end-to-end solution for the odometry estimation using CNNs and LiDAR scans.
we propose novel CNN architectures for the odometry estimation using LiDAR data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CNNs trained from sparse data can achieve comparable or even better results than state of the art methods.
CNNs trained on sparse 3D data can provide high-quality odometry estimation.
the proposed CNNs are able to learn the motion patterns and extract useful features for odometry estimation.
